description: Java enclave user_data binding of the TLSNotary proof hash + Olea nonce, via the existing tlsProof seam, with an extended JUnit test. The enclave already binds requestId/nonce/policyVersion/rawHash/transformedHash/publicKey into attestation user_data and already consumes a tlsProof map {proofType,responseHash,proofHash}. Extend the user_data binding to ALSO include the tlsProof hash (and keep the Olea nonce bound) so the Nitro attestation cryptographically commits to WHICH TLSNotary proof was presented for this request. Extend EnclaveServiceTest to assert the user_data binding now carries tlsProofHash + nonce. JDK 21, keep CID 16 / port 5005 unchanged. This depends on the tlsProof contract fields finalized in FEAT-001 and consumed by FEAT-002.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/context.json, this file, and FEAT-001 findings FIRST. Then read nitro-enclave/src/main/java/com/olea/dowsure/enclave/EnclaveService.java and EnclaveServiceTest.java and EnclaveMain.java (CID 16/port 5005 — do NOT change).

In EnclaveService.acquire, extend the `binding` LinkedHashMap (the exact map passed to attestationProvider.generateAttestation via canonical(binding)) to add two entries keyed consistently with what the Olea verifier expects: `tlsProofHash` = tlsProof.get("proofHash") and ensure `nonce` stays bound (already present). Keep insertion deterministic; the attestation-verifier.js validateUserData compares canonically (sorted keys) so field ORDER does not matter but field NAMES must match what the verifier binding builder uses. Do NOT change the manifest contract or other evidence fields beyond adding the user_data binding entry.

If the Olea attestation binding object in sam/olea/functions/verification/index.js (the 6-field binding passed to verifyNitroAttestation) must also learn tlsProofHash for validateUserData to keep matching, add tlsProofHash to that binding object in index.js as a minimal, non-breaking addition (this is the tlsProof seam, allowed). Keep rawHash/transformedHash/publicKey/requestId/nonce/policyVersion intact. Ensure the Java binding and the JS binding object are byte-identical after canonicalization.

Extend EnclaveServiceTest: update bindsTlsProofToRawResponseAndProducesManifest (or add a new test) to decode nothing (the fake provider returns the user_data bytes it was given) — instead capture the user_data passed into the AttestationProvider by using a capturing fake provider, then assert the canonical user_data JSON contains the bound nonce AND the tlsProofHash equal to the proof's proofHash. Keep the existing rejectsTlsHashMismatch test green.
Run `mvn -f nitro-enclave/pom.xml test` and confirm BUILD SUCCESS with all EnclaveServiceTest cases green (JDK 21).
Commit locally on branch tlsnotary-mpc-flow (do not push).

Record in findings: the exact user_data binding field names and order used by the Java enclave AND the matching JS binding object in index.js, so FEAT-004's end-to-end run uses an identical binding when it feeds responseHash + nonce into the enclave path and then through the Olea verifier.
acceptance_criteria: EnclaveService.acquire binds tlsProofHash and the Olea nonce into attestation user_data (alongside existing rawHash/transformedHash/publicKey/requestId/policyVersion).
The JS attestation binding object stays canonically identical to the Java user_data so verifyNitroAttestation's validateUserData still matches (no ATTESTATION_BINDING_INVALID for a valid request).
`mvn -f nitro-enclave/pom.xml test` passes with an EnclaveServiceTest assertion that the user_data carries nonce + tlsProofHash, and the existing mismatch test still passes.
verification: From the worktree root run `mvn -f nitro-enclave/pom.xml test` and confirm BUILD SUCCESS and the user_data binding test (nonce + tlsProofHash) is green.
Confirm EnclaveMain.java still binds CID 16 / port 5005 (diff shows no change there).

findings.java_user_data_binding: EnclaveService.acquire builds the `binding` LinkedHashMap in this insertion order: requestId, nonce, policyVersion, rawHash, transformedHash, publicKey, tlsProofHash. tlsProofHash = tlsProof.get("proofHash") (the self-consistent proof hash already verified earlier in acquire). The map is serialized via canonical(binding) (TreeMap sorted-key JSON) and passed as the user_data bytes to attestationProvider.generateAttestation(userDataBytes, publicKeyEncoded). nonce was already bound and is retained.
findings.js_binding_object: sam/olea/functions/verification/index.js submitEvidence passes to verifyNitroAttestation(..., binding) the object {requestId: body.requestId, nonce: body.nonce, policyVersion: body.policyVersion, rawHash: body.rawPayloadDigest, transformedHash: body.transformedPayloadDigest, publicKey: body.attestedPublicKeyBase64, tlsProofHash: body.tlsProofHash}. attestation-verifier.js validateUserData canonicalizes both sides (sorted keys) with JSON.stringify(canonicalJson(...)), so field ORDER is irrelevant but the 7 field NAMES must match exactly.
findings.field_name_mapping: Java binding key -> JS binding key / source: requestId->requestId(body.requestId); nonce->nonce(body.nonce); policyVersion->policyVersion(body.policyVersion); rawHash->rawHash(body.rawPayloadDigest); transformedHash->transformedHash(body.transformedPayloadDigest); publicKey->publicKey(body.attestedPublicKeyBase64); tlsProofHash->tlsProofHash(body.tlsProofHash). The enclave emits evidence.tlsProofHash = tlsProof.proofHash which the submitter forwards as body.tlsProofHash, so Java user_data tlsProofHash === JS binding tlsProofHash. The two canonicalize byte-identically (both sort keys), so validateUserData matches for a valid request (no ATTESTATION_BINDING_INVALID).
findings.test: EnclaveServiceTest.bindsNonceAndTlsProofHashIntoAttestationUserData uses a capturing fake AttestationProvider (AtomicReference<byte[]>) that records the exact user_data bytes passed to generateAttestation, parses them as JSON, and asserts user_data.nonce == 'n1' and user_data.tlsProofHash == the proof's proofHash. The existing bindsTlsProofToRawResponseAndProducesManifest and rejectsTlsHashMismatch tests stay green.
findings.unchanged: CID 16 / port 5005 unchanged in EnclaveMain.java. No manifest contract or other evidence fields changed; only the user_data `binding` map gained tlsProofHash and the JS binding object gained the matching tlsProofHash entry (tlsProof seam only).
findings.verification_run: mvn -f nitro-enclave/pom.xml test (JDK 21.0.11, Maven 3.9.16) -> BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0.
